title: Arriba Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Arriba wells have a median depth of 86 feet, with typical completed-well costs modeled at $9,000-$16,700.
h1: What Arriba Wells Are Really Like
intro_html:
For rural property near Arriba, the local well records point to relatively shallow wells in plains alluvium and sedimentary rock. Among permitted wells within five miles, the median reported depth is 86 feet, and the middle half runs from 64 to 100 feet. Reported yields are generally useful, but the available yield sample is small: only 19 wells report a pump yield.

That makes the nearby permit map valuable, but not a substitute for a site-specific estimate. Look at neighboring wells, the intended household or stock use, and the lot's septic and access constraints before you buy or build.

sections.heading: Arriba well depth: shallow by local standards
sections.html:
Arriba's recorded wells are mostly shallow. Sixty-nine percent are under 100 feet, while the middle half falls between 64 and 100 feet. The deepest well in the records is 200 feet, and no recorded wells fall in the 300-to-600-foot or deeper categories.

For a driller's bid, that depth pattern is useful but not a guarantee. A median well around 86 feet gives a reasonable planning point for ordinary plains ground. Local changes in alluvium, sedimentary rock, or fractured bedrock can still move the final depth. Compare nearby permits around Arriba, Flagler, and Genoa rather than relying on one parcel's closest well.

sections.heading: What Arriba wells produce
sections.html:
The reported yield median is 15.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 11.0 to 38.5 gallons per minute. In the available records, 53% report more than 15 gallons per minute, 37% fall from 5 to 15 gallons per minute, and 11% fall from 1 to 5 gallons per minute. None report less than 1 gallon per minute.

That is a favorable local yield picture, but it is based on only 19 reported pump yields. Ask for the well test, recovery information, storage design, and permitted use. A strong pump rate does not automatically establish legal availability for irrigation or other expanded uses.

sections.heading: Water levels near Arriba and what the records show
sections.html:
Only 3 wells report a static water level, so the local water-level sample is limited. Those records show a median depth to water of 70 feet, with the middle half from 54 to 74 feet. This gives a planning reference for pump setting and construction, not a dependable measurement for every lot.

The available facts do not provide enough water-level observations by decade to call a dropping or stable water table. A buyer should have the driller review nearby static levels and confirm the expected seasonal conditions. The named aquifers are split between unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifer wells and Ogallala wells; no recorded wells use a Denver Basin aquifer.

sections.heading: Arriba permit history and the drillers on record
sections.html:
The records include 189 permitted wells, with 81 recorded as constructed and 110 reporting a total depth. Activity is uneven across the decades: the largest group is the 2010s with 61 permits, followed by the 1980s and 1990s with 23 each. The newest permit year is 2024.

Eastwood Drilling, listed with Eastwood, Francis, appears most often with 26 wells. Authorized, listed with Pe and Pg, appears on 20, and Hamacher Well Works Inc, listed with Hamacher, Alan Ray, appears on 10. These are permit-record names, not a guarantee of current availability or a recommendation. Confirm licensing, insurance, scope, and references before signing.

sections.heading: What a new well may cost near Arriba
sections.html:
The local cost model assumes alluvium and plains sedimentary rock at roughly $35 to $55 per foot. At the 86-foot median depth, the drilled hole models at about $3,000 to $4,700. That is only the hole. A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at about $9,000 to $16,700.

Use those figures as a budgeting range, not a bid. A written proposal should state the drilling depth allowance, casing and grout, pump size, testing, electrical distance, trenching, permits, and what happens if the hole must go deeper or is unsuccessful. Long access routes or difficult building sites can add work beyond the well itself.

sections.heading: Risks to check before buying an Arriba lot
sections.html:
The records show 0 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 0 historic mine features, and 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites mapped within about 10 miles. That is useful screening information, but it does not prove a particular well is safe. Test the existing water for bacteria, nitrate, and other contaminants recommended for the property's setting.

Low-yield and dry-hole risk cannot be eliminated by a nearby median. Confirm the well's construction, casing, grout, pump performance, and water quality. Check septic setbacks, available replacement-area requirements, driveway access for a rig, and the proposed building footprint. Domestic and household uses make up 22% of permits, while stock use makes up 30%; the permit must match your intended use.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Arriba, Colorado?
faq.a: Wells within five miles of Arriba have a median reported depth of 86 feet. The middle half ranges from 64 to 100 feet, and 69% are under 100 feet. The deepest recorded well is 200 feet. Those figures support planning for a relatively shallow well, but local geology and the exact lot can still change the drilling depth.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Arriba?
faq.a: The local model uses $35-$55 per foot. At the 86-foot median depth, the drilled hole is modeled at about $3,000-$4,700. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at $9,000-$16,700. Get a written bid that identifies casing, grout, testing, electrical distance, and costs if drilling goes deeper.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce near Arriba?
faq.a: Among the 19 wells with reported pump yields, the median is 15.0 gallons per minute and the middle half ranges from 11.0 to 38.5 gallons per minute. Fifty-three percent report more than 15 gallons per minute. The sample is limited, so request the neighboring well test and confirm the permitted use before depending on that production.

faq.q: Is well water safe in Arriba, Colorado?
faq.a: Mapped screening records show 0 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 0 historic mine features, and 0 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites within about 10 miles. That does not certify individual well water. Test the well for bacteria, nitrate, and other locally appropriate contaminants, especially before drinking it or using it for a new household.

faq.q: What should I check before buying land with a well near Arriba?
faq.a: Review the well permit, construction report, pump test, static water level, water-quality results, and permitted use. Arriba records show a median static water depth of 70 feet, but only 3 wells report static levels. Also confirm septic setbacks, access for drilling equipment, electrical routing, and whether the existing well supports your planned household, stock, or other use.
